title: Organizing a Medium-Sized Django Application
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of organizing a medium-sized django application and at least two listed subtopics.
Interpret the organizing a medium-sized django application example and predict its expected result.
Choose a verification step and identify one version, security, data, or troubleshooting consideration.

content.intro: Learn organizing a medium-sized django application through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Organizing a Medium-Sized Django Application matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines organizing a medium-sized django application as part of advanced django architecture. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: App boundaries; Domain-focused modules; Shared utilities; Dependency direction; Avoiding unnecessary complexity. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
